newsitem.title: USA: US manufacturers group sees higher profits in 1997.
newsitem.headline: US manufacturers group sees higher profits in 1997.

text.p: Small businesses generally expect to post higher sales and profits, maintain or increase staff levels and pay slightly higher wages in 1997, according to a survey by the National Association of Manufacturers.
Of 1,600 respondents, 74 percent said they expected increased sales in 1997 over 1996, while 54 percent predicted higher profitability in 1997.
The survey showed 56 percent of respondents expect to increase capital investment in 1997, which NAM president Jerry Jasinowski cited as a key to small businesses' continuing success.
"Smaller manufacturing enterprises are seeing the benefits of increased capital investment and higher productivity, making them highly competitive in the global marketplace," Jasinowski said.
About equal numbers of participants saw constant employment (45.9 percent) as expected to increase payrolls (46.4 percent) in 1997.
Those workers will be getting paid more in 1997, with 64 percent of NAM members seeing wage increases of up to five percent and 22.6 percent seeing increases of more than five percent.

"Wages are holding at levels consistent with stable inflation," said Jasinowski. "Overall compensation to employees, however, is increasing as more and more companies offer 401k plans, profit-sharing (70.5 percent) and bonuses (72.9 percent)."
Regarding inventories, 74 percent of respondents said they expected to hold at or near current levels in 1997.
On tax issues, NAM members heavily favored a cut in the capital gains tax, eliminating estate taxes and a permanent tax credit for research and development.
